描述_EN: in 1126 the hebei province experienced great change as the northern song dynasty ended and the jin dynasty established power. porcelains differ from other ceramics in their impermeability, whiteness after firing and fine texture. the term porcelain is applied to ceramics made from a mixture containing a clay called kaolin and a white stone called petuntse, which was fired at high temperatures. this bowl is an example of ding ware, made in the hebei province of china during the northern song dynasty (960-1127) and jin dynastsy (1115-1127). from the beginning of the jin dynasty, the characteristics of ding wares changed slightly. ding wares were of the earliest true porcelains made in china, and the world. despite such upheaval, ding wares continued to be produced after a short interval as an ‘official ware’, meaning it was selected to supply ceramics to the royal household and the most elite officials in china. instead of the hand-incised decorations which previously adorned its surfaces, its designs began to mimic that of the metal wares of the period through the use of moulded design. the elaborate scene on this dish, portraying two spotted deer amongst swirling clouds and flowers, would have been slow and expensive to achieve without the precision afforded by the mould technique. this was achieved by shaping the clay over domed moulds, which gave the form of the object and impressed the inside pattern onto the clay in one step.
描述_ZN: 1126年，随着北宋王朝的结束和金朝政权的建立，河北经历了巨大的变化。 瓷器与其他陶瓷的不同之处在于其不渗透性、烧制后的白度和精细的纹理。 瓷器这一术语适用于由一种叫做高岭土的粘土和一种叫做petuntse的白色石头的混合物制成的陶瓷，在高温下烧制。 此碗是一个鼎器的例子，在北宋（960-1127）和金代（1115-1127）期间在中国的河北制造。 从金代开始，鼎器的特征发生了微小的变化。 丁器是中国乃至世界上最早的真正的瓷器。 尽管发生了这样的动荡，但在短暂的间隔之后，鼎器作为 "官器 "继续生产，这意味着它被选中为皇家和中国最精英的官员提供陶瓷。 取代了以前装饰在其表面的手工刻画的装饰，其设计开始通过使用模制设计来模仿当时的金属器皿。 这个盘子上精心设计的场景，描绘了两只斑点鹿在旋转的云彩和花朵中，如果没有模具技术提供的精确性，那么实现起来就会很慢而且很昂贵。 这是通过在圆顶模具上塑造粘土来实现的，它赋予了物品的形式，并将里面的图案一步步地印在粘土上。
